technical_errors: Internal inconsistency / dead handoff on the 'host tb' report field (lines 234, 194-204 vs. 138-142). Step 3 states as a rule: 'Capture overhead and host-testbench stall are only separable by comparison runs, which are handoffs' (lines 141-142). Step 6 honors this for capture with an explicit handoff sentence ('ask the engineer to repeat the same test on the same compile with capture disabled... The difference in steady rate is the capture term', lines 188-190). Step 7, covering host-testbench stall, never issues an equivalent handoff — it only classifies the *shape* of degradation (flat vs. monotonically decaying, lines 200-204), which identifies which mechanism is likely responsible but produces no number. By the skill's own rule in step 3 ('Only terms with a number behind them get attributed; everything else stays in the residual, named'), an unmeasured host-testbench stall should fold into `residual`, yet step 9's template offers `host tb` as an independent `<share, and the evidence line>` (line 234) with no step ever telling the reader how to derive that share. A reader following the steps literally cannot fill this field with a number and has no instruction to leave it as residual either — two engineers will resolve this differently.

The `dominant` field (line 237, values design-step|transactor|capture|host-testbench|fixed-cost|residual) can never legitimately resolve to `host-testbench` given the gap above, since that term never gets a number under the procedure as written — a second symptom of the same gap.
verb_honesty: Clean — no bare Run/Execute/Merge/Compute performed by the agent. The intro explicitly disclaims doing anything live: 'it cannot launch the emulator, enable a profiler, or time anything itself' (line 30), and step 2's 'Never open the run log with Read first' (line 79) is a locating instruction, not an execution one.

Step titles that could look suspicious on a skim — 'Measure a rate over a window' (line 110), 'Count the transactor round-trips' (line 161), 'Bound the design-step term' (line 144) — all resolve, on reading the body, to simple arithmetic (a difference, a division, a multiplication) performed on numbers already returned verbatim by a prior Grep/Read, not to the agent operating any instrument. This is the same pattern the golden reference dv-sim-log-first-error uses when it 'normalises' a signature from grepped text. Not a violation.

Every place real measurement is needed (round-trip latency, capture cost, compile achieved rate when no report exists) is correctly routed to an explicit handoff: step 5 line 175 'ask the emulation lead for the measured one', step 6 line 188 'ask the engineer to repeat the same test... with capture disabled', step 4 line 157 'ask the engineer for the path to the report'. No fabricated shortcut around any of these.
hallucination_risks: None found at high confidence. No emulator vendor name, tool flag, message string, or file default is stated outside a [[FILL:]] slot; every team-specific fact (platform, run area, progress-line format, round-trip idiom, trace config, etc.) is correctly slotted.

The domain generalizations used instead of invented specifics — clock-domain ratio and internally-generated clocks holding down achieved rate (lines 151-155), blocking vs. pipelined/streaming transactor classification (lines 170-173), front-door vs. back-door memory preload (line 264), capture cost varying by platform (line 273) — are standard, vendor-agnostic emulation knowledge, not proprietary lookup. Low risk, no action needed.
budget_violations: The 'Round-trip idiom' slot (line 54) is defined only as a call-name string to search for — unlike its sibling slots, it has no location component ('Compile report' at line 52 names a location, 'Trace configuration' at line 55 names a file, 'Host testbench' at line 56 names 'where its source lives'). Step 5's Grep for it is scoped only to 'the design-side and host-side sources' (line 165) with no directory. The retrieval budget's only stated hit-count safeguard — 'If the progress-line Grep returns more than about 200 hits, do not read them; sample the first, middle and last' (budget item 5, lines 87-88) — is explicitly scoped to the progress-line Grep only. Nothing bounds what happens if the round-trip-idiom Grep (or the step 7 host-testbench Grep) returns a large number of hits across an unscoped source tree, which is exactly the kind of Grep most likely to do so in a real SoC/IP repo. Fix: either add a location clause to the 'Round-trip idiom' slot (mirroring 'Host testbench'), or extend the >200-hit sampling rule to cover all six budgeted Greps, not just the progress-line one.
review.open_twice: "Yes. Despite being over the length budget, the retrieval-budget accounting is unusually tight and self-consistent (six Greps and five Reads, each individually traced to a step, matching the stated caps exactly — better than most skills in this pack), the domain reasoning (fixed pre-progress/post-progress cost, blocking vs. pipelined transactor stall, compile-side clock/memory causes, capture cost varying by platform) is technically sound and matches the golden reference's density and voice, and the honest-residual framing is exactly the right instinct for this problem. A senior emulation engineer would bookmark it. The host-tb dead-handoff gap and the length overage are the two things worth fixing before it ships, not reasons to discard it."

recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 clean, the retrieval budget is genuinely airtight (6 Greps declared / 6 spent, 1 Glob, 5 Reads all sited), all 10 slots are spent, metadata role/level are exactly emulation-engineer/senior-staff, and nothing unknowable is asserted outside a FILL slot. It fails on the transactor term — the one stall term the skill claims is measurable from files. The handoff line `transactor : <share, round-trip count times the platform's round-trip latency>` hardcodes the blocking-case arithmetic that step 5 itself says is wrong for a pipelined or streaming transactor ("wall clock scales with queue stalls, not with the count"), and unlike `capture` and `host tb` it offers no unmeasured/bounded spelling, so step 5's own "bounded by an unestablished latency" outcome has nowhere to be written and `dominant : transactor` can rest on a fabricated product. Compounding it, the count's first factor is unsourced: "call sites per transaction times transactions" — no step ever obtains call-sites-per-transaction, the Grep yields static call sites across every transactor variant in the directory, and the windowed Read there is spent classifying blocking vs pipelined. Separately, `fixed cost` offers "queue wait", which step 1 says the run log does not carry and which no step or handoff obtains, and `dominant` may name `fixed-cost`, a term deliberately outside step 3's window identity, with no rule making a per-job number commensurable with window shares. An engineer following the block produces a headline verdict from arithmetic the skill's own procedure contradicts.
remaining: Step 9 handoff: `transactor : <share, round-trip count times the platform's round-trip latency>` hardcodes the blocking-case formula, contradicting step 5's own 'pipelined or streaming — the design keeps clocking; wall clock scales with queue stalls, not with the count'. For a streaming transactor the product is not the stall and will typically exceed the whole window.

Step 9 handoff: `transactor` is the only measured term with no 'or unmeasured — then it sits in residual' spelling, even though step 5 explicitly produces that outcome ('If neither exists, report the count and say the term is bounded by an unestablished latency'). `capture` and `host tb` both carry the escape; transactor does not.

Step 5: 'Round-trips over the window are roughly call sites per transaction times transactions' — no step obtains 'call sites per transaction'. The Grep returns static call sites across every transactor variant in the scoped directories (one hit whether the site sits in a loop or a dead branch), and the windowed Read at the busiest site is spent classifying blocking vs pipelined, not deriving crossings per transaction.

Step 9 handoff: `fixed cost : <... load, preload, flush, copy-out, queue wait>` offers a value no step assigns. Step 1 states the queue wait is what 'the queue's accounting counts and the run log does not'; no slot names the queue accounting, Run area covers only log/summary/performance report, and there is no handoff asking the engineer for it.

Step 9 handoff: `dominant` may be `fixed-cost`, but step 3's identity is explicitly 'wall clock over the measured window = design-step + transactor + capture + host-testbench + residual' and the block defines fixed cost as 'per-job cost outside the window'. No step scales window shares to progress-phase seconds, so the dominance comparison mixes two denominators; the verification bullet 'shares sum to at most the window' only polices the in-window five.
Retrieval budget item 6 says the agent needs a capture database's 'path, size and whether they exist' — Read, Grep and Glob cannot return a file size, and no step or block field consumes one.

Step 9: '`run id`, `evidence`, `coverage` and `notes` match `dv-sim-log-first-error` and `dv-ral-bringup`' is true only of dv-ral-bringup. dv-sim-log-first-error's block (lines 200-208) carries `run id` and `notes` only — it has no `evidence` field and states coverage as prose under the block.
